_comment: What each served model is worth, so the orchestrating model can pick one per sub-agent.
WHO READS IT. The spawn-agent server, once at start-up: for every model the endpoint
lists in /v1/models it renders one line of this data into the description of its
`model` argument. The orchestrator reads that line and decides; nothing here decides
for it.
SCORES ARE COMPARABLE OR ABSENT. Every score in one category comes from ONE harness
run on every model (see _scale), never from vendor model cards: vendors each publish
different benchmarks under different settings, and a column mixing them ranks the
harnesses, not the models. A category no common source covers stays null and is
rendered 'n/a' -- a guess would be read as a measurement.
SPEED IS ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED. Decoding is memory-bandwidth bound, so its relative
cost is about active_params_b x bytes per weight (see _weight_bytes). Dense models
activate every parameter; MoE models only their active ones. The estimate ignores the
hardware each model is served on.
MATCHING is the same as vllm_model_profiles.json: the longest key that prefixes the
served id, its last path segment or any segment, '_' and '.' being one separator.
A served model with no entry is still offered, marked 'no data'.
arch                 'dense' | 'moe'
total_params_b       total parameters, billions
active_params_b      parameters used per decoded token, billions (= total if dense)
weights              served precision, a key of _weight_bytes
context_tokens       documented window; the endpoint's max_model_len wins when it has one
delegable            false = listed but refused as a sub-agent model (say why in note)
scores               {category: {benchmark: value} | null}, categories from _scale
scored_variant       the variant the source measured, when it differs from how a
sub-agent runs it (sub-agents run at the lowest reasoning rung)
sources              where each number was read, with the date
note                 anything the numbers do not say

_scale.source: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, read 2026-09-19

discovery.use: reading a lot and reporting it without inventing

glm-5.3-flash-nvfp4.note: Scores are for the unquantized model; the NVFP4 checkpoint is RedHat's quantization of it.

sources: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (552B backbone, 16B active in decode, 8B in prefill; read 2026-09-19)
deepseek-v4.1-flash.note: active_params_b is the decode figure, the one that sets generation speed. Weights assumed to be the native F8_E4M3 checkpoint.

mistral-medium-3.5-128b.note: Weights assumed BF16: the served id carries no quantization suffix.

qwen3-0.6b.note: Too small to hold a tool-calling loop: the fastest model here, and the wrong one for any sub-agent.
